subject: physics
title: Sound: pitch, loudness and speed
key_idea: Sound is made by vibrating sources and needs a medium to travel through. A higher frequency gives a higher pitch, and a larger amplitude gives a louder sound. (Supplement) Sound travels fastest in solids and slowest in gases.

blocks.text: Every sound starts with something vibrating. This section covers how sound is made and what it needs in order to travel.

items: A vibrating object, such as a guitar string, a drum skin or a loudspeaker cone, makes the air next to it vibrate.
The vibrations travel through the air as a sound wave and reach your ear.
Sound is a longitudinal wave, made of compressions and rarefactions.

items.meaning: The material a wave travels through, such as air, water or steel.

items: Sound needs a **medium**, because its vibrations are passed on from particle to particle.
There is no medium in a vacuum, so sound cannot travel through it.
This is why we can see light from the Sun but cannot hear any sound from it.
Sound is produced by vibrating sources.
Sound needs a medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

blocks.text: Two properties of the wave decide how a sound seems to the listener: its frequency and its amplitude.

items.meaning: The number of vibrations each second, measured in hertz (Hz).
The maximum displacement of the vibrating particles from their rest position.
How high or low a sound is. It depends on the frequency of the source.

items: A higher frequency of vibration gives a **higher pitch**.
A lower frequency gives a lower pitch.
A larger amplitude of vibration gives a **louder** sound.
A smaller amplitude gives a quieter sound.

diagram.alt: A slider showing a wave. Changing the amplitude changes its height, which is the loudness. Changing the frequency changes how close together the waves are, which is the pitch.

items: Higher frequency means higher pitch.
Larger amplitude means louder sound.
Changing the loudness does not change the pitch.

blocks.text: (Supplement) Sound travels at different speeds in different materials. Its speed depends on how close together the particles are.

diagram.alt: A comparison of how sound travels in a solid, a liquid and a gas.
items: Solid
Liquid

(Supplement) In general, sound travels faster in solids than in liquids, and faster in liquids than in gases.
(Supplement) Vibrations pass between particles more quickly when the particles are closer together.
(Supplement) Sound is fastest in solids, then liquids, then gases.
(Supplement) Sound travels faster where the particles are closer together.

checks.q: State why sound cannot travel through a vacuum.
checks.a: Sound needs a medium to travel through. A vacuum has no particles to pass on the vibrations.

checks.q: A sound becomes louder and lower in pitch. State what happens to its amplitude and its frequency.
checks.a: The amplitude increases and the frequency decreases.

checks.q: (Supplement) Compare the speed of sound in steel with the speed in air.
checks.a: It is much faster in steel, because sound travels faster in solids than in gases.

worked_example.question: A sound wave travels through air. The sound becomes louder and of lower pitch. State what happens to the amplitude of the sound and to the frequency of the sound.
worked_example.tip: Both changes are needed for the mark.
